dedupe_keys.name: tess ng microscopic traffic simulation system

description: TESS NG is a Chinese microscopic traffic simulation system. The TOPS research group at Tongji University began developing its prototype, TESS (Tongji traffic nEtwork Simulation System), in 2006, adding models for Chinese mixed traffic such as a nonlinear multi-stimulus car-following model, lane-change and gap-acceptance models, two-dimensional intersection models and integrated motor and non-motor vehicle flow, and released the new generation TESS NG in 2017. It is now developed by Shanghai Jida Traffic Technology, which also offers TESS MESO for mesoscopic simulation, a secondary-development edition and plug-ins, and a web version. Case projects include a digital twin for traffic management at the Beijing Winter Olympics Bird's Nest, real-time simulation and control of the Hangzhou Bay Bridge, and a real-time simulation platform for 87 km of the Shanghai S32 expressway that runs 5 to 10 times faster than real time to compare incident plans. Coverage is mainly Chinese cities and expressways. Access: commercial software sold by the company; licence terms and prices are not published on the pages read. Caveats: documentation is mostly in Chinese. It supports traffic digital twins, capacity planning, incident and emergency response and work zone analysis, and is comparable to the PTV Visum suite catalogued here.
